page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a large-scale memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is driven by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors running on x86_64 architecture at 3.1 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory is scaled to 768 GB of DDR4 RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation designed to accommodate memory-intensive operations. In addition to high-capacity volatile memory, the instance bundles 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 100 Gbps baseline network interface without attached GPU acceleration.

Empirical benchmarks reflect strong multi-threaded execution and data throughput. In stress-ng testing, multi-core performance reached top-tier scores, complemented by high-bandwidth memory access across both small cached blocks (4502.68 GB/sec) and large uncached read pools (215.93 GB/sec). Application benchmarks underscore this capability, achieving 75.03 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and leading scores in PassMark database and encryption operations. Clang compilation pipelines also benefit strongly from the wide core layout. However, single-core metrics show limitations, with stress-ng single-threaded scores and single-threaded gzip compression indexing in lower performance quartiles, alongside subdued token generation rates in large language model inference tests.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the r5dn.24xlarge consolidates extensive memory arrays, broad core density, high-speed local NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps network capacity into a single node. This combination eliminates external storage latencies and reduces network bottlenecks for data-heavy operations. The server is well positioned for enterprise in-memory caches, distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, high-volume transactional systems, and large software build matrices that fully saturate concurrent threads and require local NVMe persistence.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) based on 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processors, alongside 768 GB of DDR4 system memory configured at an 8:1 GB-to-core ratio. The instance integrates 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate superior multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 75.03 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and high throughput in database workloads, though single-core execution speeds remain modest. The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy installations by bundling substantial NVMe scratch space and dedicated networking directly with compute. This configuration is particularly suited for distributed in-memory databases, real-time caching clusters, enterprise relational databases, large-scale Clang compilation pipelines, and transactional ETL workloads requiring rapid local IOPS.
